reviewed_nonblocking_limitations.problem: invariants() lists untracked files with exclude-standard, so ignored paths are never compared. The baseline ignored inventory and the governance hashes for ignored .devai files (lines 117-119) are captured but never compared again, at any boundary or at finalization. A new or changed ignored file outside the expected official outputs would go unnoticed. Examples: .devai/state/obligations.json, counters.json, scorecards, check-cache.
reviewed_nonblocking_limitations.correction: At each sensor boundary, or at least at finalization, take the ignored inventory again and diff it against the baseline. Permit only these declared classes: new store files under .devai/state/sensor-readings, the eight body paths, coverage/, .devai/local/rounds/R-0036/, and dist/build/.turbo/.vite caches. Require unchanged hashes for any other ignored .devai file. Record every delta. Stop at a boundary on any delta outside the allowlist. No cleanup.

reviewed_nonblocking_limitations.problem: Custody is checked in one direction only: every new chain artifact must exist. The reverse is not checked. A new store file without an X-bound record would only be listed, not refused. One way this happens: native persistRegenerationReading writes the reading to the store before stdout is printed. If regeneration is killed or its output cannot be parsed after persistence, readings is empty, nothing is recorded, and the runner stops leaving that file unrecorded.
reviewed_nonblocking_limitations.correction: In final custody, and in the regeneration zero-reading path, compare the new store files against the IDs seen before the run. Validate each new file with the installed schema. Record each through public sense record, which handles an existing file natively as already-recorded and adds the missing chain entry. Only then stop. At finalization, require that every new store file has a sense.readings.record entry bound to X with a matching hash, or is listed as a gap.
